newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec split haunts money managers, institute says.
newsitem.headline: Quebec split haunts money managers, institute says.

text.p: Money managers expect the Canadian dollar would drop to a low of C$1.5625 (US$0.6400) immediately following any vote by Quebec to separate from Canada, a Canadian economic institute said on Tuesday.
The Fraser Institute said its poll of 50 investment managers in Canada showed that the specter of Quebec sovereignty was continuing to haunt investment decisions.

"The uncertainty fuelled by a volatile currency could have an adverse impact on a separate Quebec's and the rest of Canada's trade flows and economic activity," said Fazil Mihlar, policy analyst at the right-leaning research body.
Fund managers also agreed that Quebec government bonds would be downgraded if voters chose "yes" in a future sovereignty referendum.
The last referendum in October 1995 saw voters narrowly defeat a proposal to establish a sovereign Quebec with economic and political ties to Canada.
Quebec has one of the highest budget-to-GDP ratios among Canada's provinces. The French-speaking province also has a debt-to-GDP ratio of 30 percent.

"The widening of the benchmark bond spreads, along with the high budget deficit/debt would increase the cost of borrowing for a separate Quebec, and further exacerbate its fiscal problems," Mihlar said.
Seventy percent of those surveyed also predicted Canadian government bonds would be downgraded if Quebec voted for sovereignty, the poll said.
"This downgrade will likely increase the cost of borrowing for Ottawa and could potentially restrict its fiscal capacity," the poll said.
